ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, officers, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the United States OFAC SDN List, and internal PEP databases. FINTRAC requires the reporting entity to establish a written compliance policy, conduct ongoing risk assessment, perform customer due diligence, identify and verify beneficial ownership, and maintain records. For a medium-risk aviation leasing company, enhanced customer due diligence is required for all transactions involving escalation of sanctions exposure, unusual payment volumes, assets originating from sanctioned jurisdictions, or counterparties politically exposed within the meaning of FINTRAC guidelines. Statutory obligations also include reporting suspicious transactions to FINTRAC and maintaining records of all UBO confirmations for at least five years after the termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises (Quebec Enterprise Register) online portal: www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Quebec law (Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11) mandates that the corporate name must be in French or have a French version as the official name, unless a statutory exception applies. Any transliteration from non-Latin scripts must be captured in a phonetic French format using acceptable Latin characters. The name must not be deceptively similar to existing entries in the register, must be clear and descriptive, and must conform to the naming requirements of Articles 11 to 17 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Where the name includes a person's name, trademark, or initials of partners, additional documentation is required. The use of numerals, symbols, and punctuation is restricted unless otherwise permitted by the Registraire.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may submit a formal written appeal to the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days from the date of refusal under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. The appeal must be accompanied by a legal memorandum (sommaire de justification) detailing: (i) the distinctiveness of the proposed name; (ii) evidence of the French-language compliance; (iii) a trade-mark search report where applicable; and (iv) a proposed alternative name in the event of partial refusal. The Registraire reviews the request within 30 business days. If refused again, the applicant may file an administrative review application before the Administrative Tribunal of Quebec (Tribunal administratif du Québec) within 60 days. A name reservation extension may be requested for an additional 60-day period by filing Form AR-1 with payment of the extension fee no later than the expiration date.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible in Quebec for a business corporation incorporated solely for aircraft engine dry leasing, provided the service includes a physical street address located within Quebec, a reception/mail handling capacity, and unrestricted access for service of process and regulatory correspondence. The registered office cannot be a post-office box or an exclusively electronic address. A commercial virtual office that provides a dedicated meeting room for directors' meetings, corporate records storage, and acceptance of registered process may satisfy the commercial substance requirements. However, if the operation develops a genuine fixed place of business in Quebec with employees or physical assets, a true physical lease will be required. For a pure leasing entity with no Québec-based employees, assets, or management activities, Quebec tax authorities and lenders may seek evidence that the registered office is not a mere shell address and that the directors exercise real oversight, which can be shown through corporate minute books, service contracts, and bank account mandates held at the virtual office location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The quantified risk of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Registraire des entreprises for the first two years post-incorporation is 5% to 10%. The risk increases to 25% if the corporation engages in related party transactions, applies for refunds, or is classified as high-risk under tax reporting. Because the aircraft engine dry leasing industry is capital intensive and often qualifies for investment tax credits, officials may inspect the registered office to verify that administrative substance actually exists. Lenders and major aircraft lessees are also likely to conduct a pre-closing site audit at the registered office location, which more than 80% of funders perform for off-balance-sheet leasing transactions.

incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Business Registry, REQ)

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued for nominal consideration (typically C$1 per Class A common share); no escrow or capital lock-up requirement applies to this non-regulated aircraft engine dry-leasing corporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online name search and reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search request in the REQ online portal to verify the proposed French-language corporate name against the Quebec enterprise register; obtain a 90-day name reservation certificate; if a numeric-name incorporation is preferred, this step is waived.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name in French (with optional English version)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or found confusingly similar, add a distinguishing element to the proposed name and re-file the reservation request within 30 days; a notice of refusal may be contested before the Chief Registrar under QBCA s. 11.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in French (or bilingual) per QBCA s. 21; define share classes and transfer restrictions, number of first directors, and place of registered office in Quebec; obtain each incorporator's signature and each first director's written consent to act.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation (QBCA Form A-1)
Consent to act as director (formulaire de consentement des administrateurs)
Identification documents for directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of non-conformity (e.g., missing signature, insufficient French), rectify the articles and resubmit; REQ provides a pre-filing document verification service to prevent rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Registration Dossier and Pay State Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the executed articles electronically through REQ's online services; pay the C$375 incorporation fee; declare the registered office address and first directors; confirm the mandatory registrant statement; retain the electronic transmission receipt.
required_dossiers: Proof of fee payment (C$375 / approx. US$280)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For refusal, REQ sends a refusal notice with reasons; the incorporator may file an amended application or request an administrative review before the Chief Registrar within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Register with Tax Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: REQ; Revenu Québec; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, obtain the registre d'entreprise number (NEQ); register with Revenu Québec for GST/HST and employer accounts (if hiring); file CRA Form RC1 for GST/HST and payroll, or confirm eligibility for the small-supplier exemption (threshold C$30,000 for taxable supplies).
required_dossiers: Final Articles of Incorporation and directors list
Proof of registered office address (lease or ownership)
Federal GST/HST registration form (RC1) and Revenu Québec LM-1 form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registrations are filed late, submit an adjusted registration application with explanatory letter; voluntary GST/HST registration may take effect up to 30 days before the request; penalties may be waived under CRA administrative policy for first-time errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Meeting and Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (internal governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or adopt unanimous written resolutions: adopt the by-laws, ratify share allotments, appoint officers, approve banking resolutions and share certificate form, and confirm the registered office address; record all actions in the minute book and securities register (registre des valeurs mobilières).
required_dossiers: Share certs for each Class A shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any approval is omitted, pass a retroactive written resolution of directors or shareholders under QBCA s. 137 within the same fiscal year to cure the defect.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Transport Canada Civil Aviation (TCCA) — for equipment registration only; municipal building inspection service for commercial premises; no provincial licensing board governs pure aircraft engine dry leasing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — dry leasing of turbofan engines does not require an Air Operator Certificate (AOC) under Canadian Aviation Regulations (CARs 700-705); a municipal business/occupancy permit (permis d'exploitation) is required for any physical office or warehouse premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Quebec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration/Exempt — administrative declaration under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment (REAFIE, CQLR c Q-2, r. 23) is sufficient for an office/warehouse asset-leasing operation; full impact assessment is not triggered absent engine maintenance or valving activities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office/warehouse discharges to municipal sewers must meet local by-law limits: pH 6.0-9.5, total suspended solids (TSS) ≤ 500 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 100 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L; halocarbon/VOC emissions from stored engine residues subject to the Quebec Regulation respecting halocarbons (CQLR c E-12.1, r. 18.1); used oils, coolants and contaminated engine residues must be handled as hazardous waste under the Regulation respecting hazardous materials, CQLR c Q-2, r. 32, and transferred to a permitted collector.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the municipal fire prevention service (Service de prévention des incendies) for any warehouse or engine storage area; structural load certification for elevated engine storage racks and dunnage; workplace health and safety clearance from CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail) including a prevention program, and crane/lifting equipment inspection if engine handling devices are operated.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)/Agence du revenu du Canada, GST/HST; portal 'My Business Account' (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html). Provincial: Revenu Québec, Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and provincial corporate taxes; portal 'CléSécuriQ' (https://www.revenuquebec.ca). Quebec-based registrants file combined GST/HST and QST returns with Revenu Québec under the federal-provincial tax collection agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Business Corporation (federal or Quebec) engaging in aircraft-engine dry leasing: (1) incorporate federally or provincially and obtain a 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) through the Register for a Business Number service; online issuance is immediate, mail/fax (Form RC1) takes 4–8 weeks. (2) Register with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec within 60 days of beginning activity in Quebec to obtain a 10-digit NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec) and the Quebec establishment file. (3) Open GST/HST program account (code 'RT') with CRA; because the business has a permanent establishment in Quebec, register for QST with Revenu Québec (single combined registration; Form LM-1 or CléSécuriQ). (4) Submit certified constitutive documents (articles/letters patent, by-laws, directors' list, registered office address in Quebec, power of attorney) and, if a non-resident director/signatory, a CRA Form RC59 and the statutory representation mandate. (5) A mandatory licence is not required for dry engine leasing (requires_statutory_license=false); however, the engine must be cleared through CBSA on import/export, and Export Control List (EPC) permits must be obtained if the engine/technical data is listed. (6) Obtain a Canadian banking account and, for ITC purposes, preserve the registration certificate and QST/GST numbers on all invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election; entity classification follows statute/creation law, and hybrid arrangements are constrained by ITA Part XVIII hybrid mismatch rules (ss. 320.1–320.03) and transfer-pricing/arm's-length rules (ITA s.247). Relevant elections: (i) ETA s.156 election (and mirror QST provision) by which a lessor and lessee who are both registrants may deem a lease of tangible goods (aircraft engines) to be a sale at a stipulated time for GST/QST purposes; (ii) election under ETA s.156? hmm, careful. Actually ETA s.156 is 'Election to treat supply by way of lease as supply by way of sale'? Yes it is. (iii) joint ITA s.216? Not for a Canadian corp. I'll mention: (ii) optional joint election under ETA s.156/QST art. 466? for deemed sale; (iii) the 'small supplier' voluntary registration election (ETA s.240(3) and QST mirror) allowing the lessor to register before exceeding the C$30,000 threshold; (iv) for cross-border related-property leasing, an APA/advance pricing agreement and, where relevant, the hybrid-mismatch exemptions (structured arrangement exemption) must be documented.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a free currency regime. Both capital and current account transactions are fully convertible. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted without restriction, subject only to standard tax reporting and anti-money laundering compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement for mandatory surrender of export proceeds. Canadian residents must report all foreign exchange transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 to the Bank of Canada under the Bank of Canada Act. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency or converted to CAD at prevailing market rates.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for cross-border digital treasury platforms such as Wise Business or equivalent fintech services, subject to Canadian regulatory approval and full AML/KYC compliance. Offshore digital EMIs are permitted for Canadian residents with appropriate documentation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding with video KYC and document upload is permitted for standard corporate accounts. Physical presence is not mandatory but may be required for high-value transactions or enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate ownership structure chart, beneficial ownership declaration, and source of funds documentation
Enhanced due diligence reports, transaction purpose explanations, and third-party verification

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections from parent entities or shareholders are routed via SWIFT international wire transfers using purpose codes such as 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'. Verification requires board resolutions, ownership agreements, and supporting financial documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for lease payments and trade settlements are cleared via SWIFT MT103 messages or correspondent banking networks. Commercial Letters of Credit may be utilized for structured aviation asset settlements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of $25 per day up to maximum $500; prolonged non-filing may trigger administrative dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if corporation is a reporting issuer or meets public company thresholds under securities legislation; private corporations generally exempt
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP for private companies; IFRS for public or listed issuers

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of directors, shareholders and beneficial ownership; shareholding transfers require register update within 15 days
